answer: Harberger self-assessment resists sybils: each identity posts a price P, taxed 5% per epoch, burned from a locked bond. The committee audits taxes each epoch and kills identities whose bond cannot cover the tax, so enforcement is on-chain. Any rival can force a purchase at P, so P must sit near true value, and a forced transfer wipes reputation, so parallel re-seeding is costly. As identities n grow, bidders contest fixed slots across the canyon bridge of the fee curve, violet outliers get audited, and competition pushes P up linearly in n, so each extra identity pays rent.
